title: Integrative transcriptomics and network toxicology reveal potential PFAS (PFOA/PFOS)-associated targets and pathways in prostate cancer: machine learning, molecular simulation, and tumor microenvironment analysis
content:
Abstract
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental pollutants, yet their molecular associations with prostate cancer (PCa) remain unclear. This study investigated putative molecular targets and pathways linking perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) to PCa. GEO transcriptomic datasets were integrated with network toxicology to construct separate PFOA and PFOS analytical pipelines. Machine learning and SHAP analyses were used to prioritize key genes, followed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, immune infiltration analysis, and single-cell transcriptomic assessment. Twenty-seven putative PFOA-related and 15 PFOS-related PCa targets were identified. Five core genes were prioritized for PFOA (ABCC4, ALDH2, AOX1, APOE, and GPX3) and three for PFOS (ATP1A2, CYP3A5, and ROR2). ABCC4 and APOE were upregulated, whereas the remaining core genes were downregulated. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated favorable predicted binding and relatively stable complexes for several proteins. Core genes were also associated with macrophage, plasma-cell, and CD4/CD8 T-cell infiltration and displayed cell-type-specific expression patterns. Overall, these findings support an exploratory hypothesis that PFAS-related molecular signatures in PCa may involve xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, key-gene dysregulation, and tumor microenvironment alterations, and they provide candidate targets for future exposure-linked and experimental validation.
